candidate.educational_objective: Identify haloperidol decanoate as a long-acting intramuscular formulation labeled for adults with schizophrenia who were previously stabilized on immediate-release oral haloperidol.

options.A: An adult with schizophrenia who has been taking a stable dose of immediate-release oral haloperidol
options.B: A client with sudden severe agitation who needs medication to take effect within minutes
options.C: A client receiving haloperidol for the first time who has never been stabilized on oral haloperidol
options.D: An older adult with dementia-related psychosis who requires long-term behavioral control

candidate.rationale: Current DailyMed labeling states that haloperidol decanoate injection is indicated for treatment of schizophrenia in adults who were previously taking a stable dosage of an immediate-release oral haloperidol product. It is administered by deep intramuscular injection every 4 weeks. Therefore A is the best answer. B describes an acute rapid-treatment need rather than the labeled long-acting use; C omits prior stabilization on immediate-release oral haloperidol; and D is incorrect because haloperidol decanoate is not approved for dementia-related psychosis and carries a boxed warning in that population.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Haloperidol decanoate is a long-acting IM antipsychotic labeled for adults with schizophrenia previously stabilized on immediate-release oral haloperidol and administered every 4 weeks; it is not approved for dementia-related psychosis.
